usdRate.sourceName: Central Bank of Iceland official exchange rate (USD)
usdRate.note: ISK 121.73 per US dollar (EUR 136.00) on 30 October 2026, matching the ECB cross rate; World Bank 2025 average 128.44.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Statistics Iceland, consumer price index (annual change)
inflation_cpi.note: CPI 12-month rise 5.9% in October 2026 (shown on the Statistics Iceland CPI chart; the Central Bank statement of 7 October also cites 5.9%); the Central Bank target is 2.5%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Central Bank of Iceland 2.5% target; CPI 5.9% in October 2026; 2021-2025 CPI average about 6%
inflation_projection.note: Inflation has stayed above 4% since 2021 and the target has not been met for years, so planning uses 4%, between the 2.5% target and recent outcomes.

policy_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Iceland, Statement of the Monetary Policy Committee, 7 October 2026
policy_rate.note: Key rate (seven-day term deposit rate) kept at 8.00% on 7 October 2026; the statement notes inflation at 5.9% and underlying inflation just over 4%. Next decision 18 November 2026.

savings_account_rate.note: The Central Bank of Iceland publishes deposit-rate statistics only through a script-driven data portal that could not be read; no official average for this deposit type was found.

fdr_3m_rate.note: The Central Bank of Iceland publishes deposit-rate statistics only through a script-driven data portal that could not be read; no official average for this deposit type was found.

fdr_1y_rate.note: The Central Bank of Iceland publishes deposit-rate statistics only through a script-driven data portal that could not be read; no official average for this deposit type was found.

dps_rate.note: No standard monthly recurring-deposit product with a published average rate was found for Iceland.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: The Central Bank of Iceland publishes deposit-rate statistics only through a script-driven data portal that could not be read; no official average for this deposit type was found. World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no Iceland figure.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate or retail savings bond for individuals is currently sold in Iceland (Government Debt Management lists only treasury bills and nominal and indexed treasury bonds).

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Government Debt Management (Lánamál ríkisins, Central Bank of Iceland), treasury bill auction results RIKV 27 0120
tbill_91d_rate.note: 3-month bill RIKV 27 0120 (settled 14 October 2026, matures 20 January 2027) sold at 8.148% flat rate, highest accepted; 9-month RIKV 27 0721 at 8.119%.

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: Government Debt Management (Lánamál ríkisins), market overview RIKB 31 0124
tbond_5y_rate.note: Closing yield 7.42% on the nominal treasury bond maturing 24 January 2031 (about 4.2 years); RIKB 32 1015 (6 years) is not quoted on the page.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Government Debt Management (Lánamál ríkisins), market overview RIKB 35 0917
tbond_10y_rate.note: Bid yield 7.00% (last trade 6.99%) on the nominal treasury bond maturing 17 September 2035 (about 9 years); Trading Economics 10-year 7.00% on 30 October 2026.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Iceland income determination
tax_bank_interest.note: Interest is taxed at 22% capital income tax; the first ISK 300,000 of interest a year per person is exempt in the final assessment (withholding still applies).

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No government savings certificate exists in Iceland; interest on treasury bills and bonds is ordinary capital income taxed at 22% (PwC).

deposit_insurance_limit.note: Deposits are covered by the Depositors' and Investors' Guarantee Fund (TIF) under Act 98/2019, but tif.is returned 403 and the law text on althingi.is is behind a bot check, so the cover amount could not be read.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap or official average credit card rate was found; the Central Bank's interest-rate statistics could not be read.

equity_return_low.sourceName: OMX Iceland all-share index (ICEX) 1,956 on 30 Oct 2026, down 6.5% in a year and 76% below its 2007 high
equity_return_low.note: Low case: Icelandic shares continue their weak record and earn less than after-tax treasury bills.

equity_return_base.sourceName: ICEX index (Trading Economics); 3-month treasury bill 8.15% less 22% tax = 6.4%
equity_return_base.note: Base case: about 1.5 points over the after-tax bill rate, kept low because the local index has a weak record and is small and concentrated.

equity_return_high.sourceName: ICEX index (Trading Economics); global equity long-run returns plus krona depreciation
equity_return_high.note: High case: a diversified fund with global shares earning 7-8% in foreign currency plus some krona depreciation.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold USD price history (Trading Economics); ISK 121.73 per US dollar (Central Bank of Iceland)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold stalls after the 2025-26 spike and the krona holds its value.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold USD price history (Trading Economics); Icelandic inflation above trading partners
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises with world inflation plus a little, and the krona loses about 2% a year against the dollar because Icelandic inflation runs higher.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in krona terms.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Inflation-indexed treasury bonds 2.8-3.8% real (Lánamál ríkisins); CPI 5.9%
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: policy rates fall back toward 5% and after-tax returns on deposits and bills drop to about 4%.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: 3-month treasury bill 8.15% less 22% capital income tax = 6.4% (Lánamál ríkisins)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: kept below today's after-tax bill rate because the key rate is expected to fall as inflation eases.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: 5-year treasury bond 7.42% less 22% tax = 5.8%; bills 6.4% after tax
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: locking in today's high nominal yields, close to the after-tax bill rate.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The Central Bank of Iceland (insurance supervisor) does not publish an industry life claim settlement ratio that could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover is sold in Iceland, but no regulator or official premium table per sum insured was found; only individual company quotes exist.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Hospital admission is covered by Icelandic Health Insurance (Sjúkratryggingar) for residents; no official figure for an out-of-pocket cost of a major hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Residents are covered by public health insurance; private health insurance is mainly sold for the six-month waiting period of new residents (EC guide, July 2026), and no premium table was found.

oop_health_share.note: Out-of-pocket spending was 14.9% of current health expenditure in 2024 (latest available; older than 2025).

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Statistics Iceland CPI 5.9% (October 2026); Central Bank 2.5% target
goal_inflation_health.note: No separate health price index was read; health costs usually rise a little faster than general prices, so planning uses 5%, one point above the general projection.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Statistics Iceland CPI 5.9% (October 2026); Central Bank 2.5% target
goal_inflation_education.note: Public education is largely free; planning uses 4.5% for private and higher-education costs, slightly above the general projection.

life_expectancy.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_expectancy.note: Men 82.0, women 84.7 (UN WPP estimate for 2026); World Bank 2024 figure 82.8.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years computed from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP 2026 estimate).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 24.0 (2025, World Bank), 32.0 (2040) and 54.4 (2065, populationpyramid.net/iceland/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: European Commission, Your social security rights in Iceland (July 2026)
retirement_age_default.note: Public old-age pension is paid from 67 (reduced pension possible from 65); occupational pension funds generally pay from 65-67.

retirement_age_government.note: State employees are understood to leave service at 70 under Act 70/1996, but the law text on althingi.is refused automated access and no other official page stating the age was read.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: after-tax returns fall to about 4% as the key rate comes down.

retirement_return_base.note: Base case: below the after-tax treasury bill rate, allowing for lower rates over a long retirement.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: After-tax treasury bills 6.4%; 5-year bond 7.42% less tax 5.8%
retirement_return_high.note: High case: keeping today's after-tax government yields.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Fixed income low 4%; weak ICEX record
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 8% and half safe fixed income at about 5.5%, rounded up for some global diversification.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: Social Insurance Administration (Tryggingastofnun), old-age pension amounts 2026
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Full residence-based old-age pension ISK 365,592 a month before tax (40 years' residence); singles living alone also get a household supplement of up to ISK 92,384. It falls by 45% of income above the income allowance.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: European Commission, Your social security rights in Iceland (July 2026)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Paid from 67 to residents with at least 3 years' residence between 16 and 67 (full amount after 40 years); income-tested against other income including occupational pensions.

gratuity_rule.note: No statutory gratuity or end-of-service payment for private employees was found in the sources read; severance in Iceland is set by collective agreements rather than a days-per-year law, but no source confirming this was read.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: European Commission, Your social security rights in Iceland (July 2026); Social Insurance Administration
public_pension_scheme.note: Two pillars: the residence-based state pension from 67 (taxable, amounts before tax per TR) and compulsory occupational pension funds, open to all workers and payable from 65 with no residence condition. State pension amounts are raised each year in the budget; the guide does not describe the indexation rule.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring-deposit product was found.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No retail government savings certificate is currently sold; individuals can buy treasury bills and bonds through banks and brokers.

tbill_91d.note: 1- to 9-month bills auctioned monthly by Government Debt Management.

equity_fund.note: Domestic and global equity funds are available to retail investors.

insuranceRegulator.name: Central Bank of Iceland, Financial Supervision
insuranceRegulator.note: The Financial Supervisory Authority merged into the Central Bank in 2020.

insuranceComplaints.name: Central Bank of Iceland, consumer information and complaints
insuranceComplaints.note: Insurance disputes go to the Insurance Complaints Committee (Úrskurðarnefnd í vátryggingamálum), administered with the Central Bank.
